newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds end mixed on renewed Brazil worry.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds end mixed on renewed Brazil worry.

text.p: Argentine bonds ended mixed Thursday, with Bocons modestly extending their gains but Bradies dragged down by continued volatility in Brazil after rumors it could devalue its real currency, dealers said.

The market had looked firm in early trading, but losses for Brazilian stocks and bonds, exacerbated by selling of Brazil's heavily traded Telebras, spilled over into Argentina which had appeared to shrug off Brazilian worries.

"The bond market is continuing to show a firm base," said one dealer. "Local indicators are postive, but we are seeing an impasse in Brazilian markets which continues despite the denials of a real devaluation."

Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was down 1/2 at 93.875 by the close, in tune with Brazilian Bradies. The Argentine dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001, on the other hand, closed $0.05 higher on the previous day at 118.25.
